section.heading: EQUITABLE RELIEF FROM INELIGIBILITY FOR LOANS, PAYMENTS, OR OTHER BENEFITS.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Agricultural commodity.—
paragraph.content: The term “agricultural commodity” means any agricultural commodity, food, feed, fiber, or livestock that is subject to a covered program.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “covered program” means—

clause.content: a program administered by the Secretary under which price or income support, or production or market loss assistance, is provided to producers of agricultural commodities; and
a conservation program administered by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Exclusions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “covered program” does not include—

clause.content: an agricultural credit program carried out under the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 1921 et seq.); or
the crop insurance program carried out under the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 U.S.C. 1501 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Participant.—
paragraph.content: The term “participant” means a participant in a covered program.

paragraph.heading: State conservationist.—
paragraph.content: The term “State Conservationist” means the State Conservationist with respect to a program administered by the Natural Resources Conservation Service.

paragraph.heading: State director.—
paragraph.content: The term “State Director” means the State Executive Director of the Farm Service Agency with respect to a program administered by the Farm Service Agency.

subsection.heading: Equitable Relief.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may provide relief to any participant that is determined to be not in compliance with the requirements of a covered program, and therefore ineligible for a loan, payment, or other benefit under the covered program, if the participant—

paragraph.content: acting in good faith, relied on the action or advice of the Secretary (including any authorized representative of the Secretary) to the detriment of the participant; or
failed to comply fully with the requirements of the covered program, but made a good faith effort to comply with the requirements.

subsection.heading: Forms of Relief.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may authorize a participant in a covered program to—

paragraph.content: retain loans, payments, or other benefits received under the covered program;
continue to receive loans, payments, and other benefits under the covered program;
continue to participate, in whole or in part, under any contract executed under the covered program;
in the case of a conservation program, reenroll all or part of the land covered by the program; and
receive such other equitable relief as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Remedial Action.—
subsection.content: As a condition of receiving relief under this section, the Secretary may require the participant to take actions designed to remedy any failure to comply with the covered program.

subsection.heading: Equitable Relief by State Directors and State Conservationists.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: A State Director, in the case of programs administered by the State Director, and the State Conservationist, in the case of programs administered by the State Conservationist, may grant relief to a participant in accordance with subsections (b) through (d) if—

subparagraph.content: the amount of loans, payments, and benefits for which relief will be provided to the participant under this subsection is less than $20,000;
the total amount of loans, payments, and benefits for which relief has been previously provided to the participant under this subsection is not more than $5,000; and
the total amount of loans, payments, and benefits for which relief is provided to similarly situated participants under this subsection is not more than $1,000,000, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Consultation, approval, and reversal.—
paragraph.chapeau: The decision by a State Director or State Conservationist to grant relief under this subsection—

subparagraph.content: shall not require prior approval by the Administrator of the Farm Service Agency, the Chief of the Natural Resources Conservation Service, or any other officer or employee of the Agency or Service;
shall be made only after consultation with, and the approval of, the Office of General Counsel of the Department of Agriculture; and
is subject to reversal only by the Secretary (who may not delegate the reversal authority).

paragraph.heading: Nonapplicability.—
paragraph.chapeau: The authority of a State Director or State Conservationist under this subsection does not apply to the administration of—

subparagraph.chapeau: payment limitations under—

clause.content: sections 1001 through 1001F of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308 et seq.); or
a conservation program administered by the Secretary.

subparagraph.content: highly erodible land and wetland conservation requirements under subtitle B or C of title XII of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3811 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Other authority.—
paragraph.content: The authority provided to a State Director and State Conservationist under this subsection is in addition to any other applicable authority and does not limit other authority provided by law or the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Judicial Review.—
subsection.content: A discretionary decision by the Secretary, the State Director, or the State Conservationist under this section shall be final, and shall not be subject to review under chapter 7 of title 5, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Reports.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than February 1 of each year, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report that describes for the previous calendar year—

paragraph.content: the number of requests for equitable relief under subsections (b) and (e) and the disposition of the requests; and
the number of requests for equitable relief under section 278(d) of the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 6998(d)) and the disposition of the requests.

subsection.heading: Relationship to Other Law.—
subsection.content: The authority provided in this section is in addition to any other authority provided in this or any other Act.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Eligible land.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible land” means privately owned agricultural land (including land in which a State has a property interest as a result of State water law)—

subparagraph.content: that a landowner voluntarily agrees to sell to a State; and

subparagraph.chapeau: which—

subclause.content: is ineligible for enrollment as a wetland reserve easement established under the agricultural conservation easement program under subtitle H of the Food Security Act of 1985;

a level below which the State determines the management of the water level is beyond the control of the State or landowner; or

subclause.content: is inaccessible for agricultural use due to the flooding of adjoining property (such as islands of agricultural land created by flooding);

clause.content: is located within a watershed with water rights available for lease or purchase; and

clause.chapeau: has been used during at least 5 of the immediately preceding 30 years—

subclause.content: to produce crops or hay; or
as livestock pasture or grazing.

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “program” means the voluntary land purchase program established under this section.

paragraph.heading: Terminal lake.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “terminal lake” means a lake and its associated riparian and watershed resources that is—

subparagraph.content: considered flooded because there is no natural outlet for water accumulating in the lake or the associated riparian area such that the watershed and surrounding land is consistently flooded; or

considered terminal because it has no natural outlet and is at risk due to a history of consistent Federal assistance to address critical resource conditions, including insufficient water available to meet the needs of the lake, general uses, and water rights.

subsection.heading: Assistance.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: provide grants under subsection (c) for the purchase of eligible land impacted by a terminal lake described in subsection (a)(3)(A); and
provide funds to the Secretary of the Interior pursuant to subsection (e)(2) with assistance in accordance with subsection (d) for terminal lakes described in subsection (a)(3)(B).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Using funds provided under subsection (e)(1), the Secretary shall make available land purchase grants to States for the purchase of eligible land in accordance with this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: Amount.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A land purchase grant shall be in an amount not to exceed the lesser of—

clause.content: 50 percent of the total purchase price per acre of the eligible land; or

subclause.content: in the case of eligible land that was used to produce crops or hay, $400 per acre; and
in the case of eligible land that was pasture or grazing land, $200 per acre.

subparagraph.heading: Determination of purchase price.—
subparagraph.content: A State purchasing eligible land with a land purchase grant shall ensure, to the maximum extent practicable, that the purchase price of such land reflects the value, if any, of other encumbrances on the eligible land to be purchased, including easements and mineral rights.

subparagraph.heading: Cost-share required.—
subparagraph.content: To be eligible to receive a land purchase grant, a State shall provide matching non-Federal funds in an amount equal to 50 percent of the amount described in subparagraph (A), including additional non-Federal funds.

subparagraph.heading: Conditions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: To receive a land purchase grant, a State shall agree—

clause.chapeau: to ensure that any eligible land purchased is—

subclause.content: conveyed in fee simple to the State; and
free from mortgages or other liens at the time title is transferred;

clause.content: to maintain ownership of the eligible land in perpetuity;
to pay (from funds other than grant dollars awarded) any costs associated with the purchase of eligible land under this section, including surveys and legal fees; and
to keep eligible land in a conserving use, as defined by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Loss of federal benefits.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Eligible land purchased with a grant under this section shall lose eligibility for any benefits under other Federal programs, including—

clause.content: benefits under title XII of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.);
benefits under the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 U.S.C. 1501 et seq.); and
covered benefits described in section 1001D(b) of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308–3a).

subparagraph.heading: Prohibition.—
subparagraph.content: Any Federal rights or benefits associated with eligible land prior to purchase by a State may not be transferred to any other land or person in anticipation of or as a result of such purchase.

section.heading: MCGOVERN-DOLE INTERNATIONAL FOOD FOR EDUCATION AND CHILD NUTRITION PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Definition of Agricultural Commodity.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “agricultural commodity” means an agricultural commodity, or a product of an agricultural commodity, that—

paragraph.content: is produced in the United States; or

subparagraph.chapeau: is produced in and procured from—

clause.content: a developing country that is a recipient country; or
a developing country in the same region as a recipient country; and

subparagraph.content: at a minimum, meets each nutritional, quality, and labeling standard of the recipient country, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Program.—
subsection.chapeau: Subject to subsection (l), the Secretary may establish a program, to be known as “McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program”, requiring the procurement of agricultural commodities and the provision of financial and technical assistance to carry out—

paragraph.content: preschool and school food for education programs in foreign countries to improve food security, reduce the incidence of hunger, and improve literacy and primary education, particularly with respect to girls; and
maternal, infant, and child nutrition programs for pregnant women, nursing mothers, infants, and children who are 5 years of age or younger.

subsection.heading: Eligible Commodities and Cost Items.—
subsection.chapeau: Notwithstanding any other provision of law—

paragraph.content: any agricultural commodity is eligible to be provided under this section;

paragraph.chapeau: as necessary to achieve the purposes of this section, funds appropriated under this section may be used to pay—

clause.content: the cost of acquiring agricultural commodities;
the costs associated with packaging, enrichment, preservation, and fortification of agricultural commodities;
the processing, transportation, handling, and other incidental costs up to the time of the delivery of agricultural commodities free on board vessels in United States ports;
the vessel freight charges from United States ports or designated Canadian transshipment ports, as determined by the Secretary, to designated ports of entry abroad;

clause.chapeau: the costs associated with transporting agricultural commodities from United States ports to designated points of entry abroad in the case—

subclause.content: of landlocked countries;
of ports that cannot be used effectively because of natural or other disturbances;
of the unavailability of carriers to a specific country; or
of substantial savings in costs or time that may be effected by the utilization of points of entry other than ports;

clause.content: the costs associated with transporting the commodities described in subsection (a)(2) from a developing country described in subparagraph (A)(ii) of that subsection to any designated point of entry within the recipient country; and
the charges for general average contributions arising out of the ocean transport of agricultural commodities transferred pursuant thereto;

subparagraph.chapeau: all or any part of the internal transportation, storage, and handling costs incurred in moving the eligible commodity, if the Secretary determines that—

clause.content: payment of the costs is appropriate; and

clause.chapeau: the recipient country is a low income, net food-importing country that—

subclause.content: meets the poverty criteria established by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for Civil Works Preference; and

has a national government that is committed to or is working toward, through a national action plan, the goals of the World Declaration on Education for All convened in 1990 in Jomtien, Thailand, and the followup Dakar Framework for Action of the World Education Forum, convened in 2000;

subparagraph.content: the costs of activities conducted in the recipient countries by a nonprofit voluntary organization, cooperative, or intergovernmental agency or organization that would enhance the effectiveness of the activities implemented by such entities under this section; and
the costs of meeting the allowable administrative expenses of private voluntary organizations, cooperatives, or intergovernmental organizations that are implementing activities under this section.

subsection.heading: General Authorities.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: implement the program established under this section;
ensure that the program established under this section is consistent with the foreign policy and development assistance objectives of the United States; and

consider, in determining whether a country should receive assistance under this section, whether the government of the country is taking concrete steps to improve the preschool and school systems in the country.

subsection.heading: Eligible Entities.—
subsection.content: Assistance may be provided under this section to private voluntary organizations, cooperatives, intergovernmental organizations, governments of developing countries and their agencies, and other organizations.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (b), the Secretary shall ensure that procedures are established that—

subparagraph.content: provide for the submission of proposals by eligible entities, each of which may include 1 or more recipient countries, for commodities and other assistance under this section;
provide for eligible commodities and assistance on a multiyear basis;

ensure that eligible entities demonstrate the organizational capacity and the ability to develop, implement, monitor, report on, and provide accountability for activities conducted under this section;
provide for the expedited development, review, and approval of proposals submitted in accordance with this section;

subparagraph.chapeau: ensure to the maximum extent practicable that assistance—

clause.content: is provided under this section in a timely manner; and
is available when needed throughout the applicable school year;

subparagraph.content: ensure monitoring and reporting by eligible entities on the use of commodities and other assistance provided under this section; and

allow for the sale or barter of commodities by eligible entities to acquire funds to implement activities that improve the food security of women and children or otherwise enhance the effectiveness of programs and activities authorized under this section.

paragraph.heading: Priorities for program funding.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out paragraph (1) with respect to criteria for determining the use of commodities and other assistance provided for programs and activities authorized under this section, the Secretary may consider the ability of eligible entities to—

subparagraph.content: identify and assess the needs of beneficiaries, especially malnourished or undernourished mothers and their children who are 5 years of age or younger, and school-age children who are malnourished, undernourished, or do not regularly attend school;

clause.content: in the case of preschool and school-age children, target low-income areas where children's enrollment and attendance in school is low or girls' enrollment and participation in preschool or school is low, and incorporate developmental objectives for improving literacy and primary education, particularly with respect to girls; and

in the case of programs to benefit mothers and children who are 5 years of age or younger, coordinate supplementary feeding and nutrition programs with existing or newly-established maternal, infant, and children programs that provide health-needs interventions, including maternal, prenatal, and postnatal and newborn care;

subparagraph.content: involve indigenous institutions as well as local communities and governments in the development and implementation of the programs and activities to foster local capacity building and leadership; and
carry out multiyear programs that foster local self-sufficiency and ensure the longevity of programs in the recipient country .

subsection.heading: Use of Food and Nutrition Service.—
subsection.content: The Food and Nutrition Service of the Department of Agriculture may provide technical advice on the establishment of programs under subsection (b)(1) and on implementation of the programs in the field in recipient countries.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary is urged to engage existing international food aid coordinating mechanisms to ensure multilateral commitments to, and participation in, programs similar to programs supported under this section.

paragraph.heading: Reports.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall annually submit to the Committee on International Relations and the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report on the commitments and activities of governments, including the United States government, in the global effort to reduce child hunger and increase school attendance.

subsection.heading: Private Sector Involvement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary is urged to encourage the support and active involvement of the private sector, foundations, and other individuals and organizations in programs assisted under this section.

subsection.heading: Graduation.—
subsection.chapeau: An agreement with an eligible organization under this section shall include provisions—

paragraph.chapeau: to—

subparagraph.content: sustain the benefits to the education, enrollment, and attendance of children in schools in the targeted communities when the provision of commodities and assistance to a recipient country under a program under this section terminates; and
estimate the period of time required until the recipient country or eligible organization is able to provide sufficient assistance without additional assistance under this section; or

paragraph.content: to provide other long-term benefits to targeted populations of the recipient country.

subsection.heading: Requirement To Safeguard Local Production and Usual Marketing.—
subsection.content: The requirement of section 403(a) of the Food for Peace Act (7 U.S.C. 1733(a)) applies with respect to the availability of commodities under this section.

paragraph.heading: Use of commodity credit corporation funds.—
paragraph.content: Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall use to carry out this section $84,000,000 for fiscal year 2009, to remain available until expended.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.content: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as are necessary to carry out this section for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2023.

paragraph.heading: Administrative expenses.—
paragraph.content: Funds made available to carry out this section may be used to pay the administrative expenses of the Department of Agriculture or any other Federal agency assisting in the implementation of this section.

paragraph.heading: Purchase of commodities.—
paragraph.content: Of the funds made available to carry out this section, not more than 10 percent shall be used to purchase agricultural commodities described in subsection (a)(2).

paragraph.content: identifies opportunities for the growth of agricultural exports to overseas markets;
ensures that the resources, programs, and policies of the Department are coordinated with those of other agencies; and
remove barriers to agricultural trade in overseas markets.

subsection.heading: Review.—
subsection.chapeau: The consultations under subsection (a) shall include a review of—

paragraph.content: the strategic goals of the Department; and
the progress of the Department in implementing the strategic goals through the global market strategy.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS CONCERNING FOREIGN ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS.

subsection.heading: Findings.—
subsection.chapeau: Congress finds that—

paragraph.content: the international community faces a continuing epidemic of ethnic, sectarian, and criminal violence;
poverty, hunger, political uncertainty, and social instability are the principal causes of violence and conflict around the world;
broad-based, equitable economic growth and agriculture development facilitates political stability, food security, democracy, and the rule of law;
democratic governments are more likely to advocate and observe international laws, protect civil and human rights, pursue free market economies, and avoid external conflicts;

the United States Agency for International Development has provided critical democracy and governance assistance to a majority of the nations that successfully made the transition to democratic governments during the past 2 decades;
43 of the top 50 consumer nations of American agricultural products were once United States foreign aid recipients;

in the past 50 years, infant child death rates in the developing world have been reduced by 50 percent, and health conditions around the world have improved more during this period than in any other period;
the United States Agency for International Development child survival programs have significantly contributed to a 10 percent reduction in infant mortality rates worldwide in just the past 8 years;

in providing assistance by the United States and other donors in better seeds and teaching more efficient agricultural techniques over the past 2 decades have helped make it possible to feed an additional 1,000,000,000 people in the world;
despite this progress, approximately 1,200,000,000 people, one-quarter of the world's population, live on less that $1 per day, and approximately 3,000,000,000 people live on only $2 per day;
95 percent of new births occur in developing countries, including the world's poorest countries; and
only ½ percent of the Federal budget is dedicated to international economic and humanitarian assistance.

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of Congress that—

paragraph.content: United States foreign assistance programs should play an increased role in the global fight against terrorism to complement the national security objectives of the United States;

the United States should lead coordinated international efforts to provide increased financial assistance to countries with impoverished and disadvantaged populations that are the breeding grounds for terrorism; and

the United States Agency for International Development and the Department of Agriculture should substantially increase humanitarian, economic development, and agricultural assistance to foster international peace and stability and the promotion of human rights.

section.heading: SENSE OF THE SENATE CONCERNING AGRICULTURAL TRADE.

subsection.heading: Agriculture Trade Negotiating Objectives.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of the Senate that the principal negotiating objective of the United States with respect to agricultural trade in all multilateral, regional, and bilateral negotiations is to obtain competitive opportunities for the export of United States agricultural commodities in foreign markets substantially equivalent to the competitive opportunities afforded foreign exports in United States markets and to achieve fairer and more open conditions of agricultural trade in bulk and value-added commodities by—

paragraph.content: reducing or eliminating, by a date certain, tariffs or other charges that decrease market opportunities for the export of United States agricultural commodities, giving priority to United States agricultural commodities that are subject to significantly higher tariffs or subsidy regimes of major producing countries;

immediately eliminating all export subsidies on agricultural commodities worldwide while maintaining bona fide food aid and preserving United States agricultural market development and export credit programs that allow the United States to compete with other foreign export promotion efforts;

leveling the playing field for United States agricultural producers by disciplining domestic supports such that no other country can provide greater support, measured as a percentage of total agricultural production value, than the United States does while preserving existing green box category to support conservation activities, family farms, and rural communities;

paragraph.chapeau: developing, strengthening, and clarifying rules and effective dispute settlement mechanisms to eliminate practices that unfairly decrease United States market access opportunities for United States agricultural commodities or distort agricultural markets to the detriment of the United States, including—

subparagraph.chapeau: unfair or trade-distorting activities of state trading enterprises and other administrative mechanisms, with emphasis on—

clause.content: requiring price transparency in the operation of state trading enterprises and such other mechanisms; and

ending discriminatory pricing practices for agricultural commodities that amount to de facto export subsidies so that the enterprises or other mechanisms do not (except in cases of bona fide food aid) sell agricultural commodities in foreign markets at prices below domestic market prices or prices below the full costs of acquiring and delivering agricultural commodities to the foreign markets;

subparagraph.content: unjustified trade restrictions or commercial requirements affecting new agricultural technologies, including biotechnology;

unjustified sanitary or phytosanitary restrictions, including restrictions that are not based on scientific principles, in contravention of the Agreement on the Application of Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures (as described in section 101(d)(3) of the Uruguay Round Agreements Act (19 U.S.C. 3511(d)(3)));
other unjustified technical barriers to agricultural trade; and
restrictive and nontransparent rules in the administration of tariff rate quotas;

paragraph.content: improving import relief mechanisms to recognize the unique characteristics of perishable agricultural commodities;

paragraph.chapeau: taking into account whether a party to negotiations with respect to trading in an agricultural commodity has—

subparagraph.content: failed to adhere to the provisions of an existing bilateral trade agreement with the United States;
circumvented obligations under a multilateral trade agreement to which the United States is a signatory; or
manipulated its currency value to the detriment of United States agricultural producers or exporters; and

paragraph.chapeau: otherwise ensuring that countries that accede to the World Trade Organization—

subparagraph.content: have made meaningful market liberalization commitments in agriculture; and
make progress in fulfilling those commitments over time.

subsection.heading: Priority for Agriculture Trade.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of the Senate that—

paragraph.content: reaching a successful agreement on agriculture should be the top priority of United States negotiators in World Trade Organization talks; and

if the primary export competitors of the United States fail to reduce their trade distorting domestic supports and eliminate export subsidies in accordance with the negotiating objectives expressed in this section, the United States should take steps to increase the leverage of United States negotiators and level the playing field for United States producers, within existing World Trade Organization commitments.

subsection.heading: Consultation With Congressional Committees.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of the Senate that—

paragraph.content: before the United States Trade Representative negotiates a trade agreement that would reduce tariffs on agricultural commodities or require a change in United States agricultural law, the United States Trade Representative should consult with the Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Ways and Means of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry and the Committee on Finance of the Senate;

paragraph.chapeau: not less than 48 hours before initialing an agreement relating to agricultural trade negotiated under the auspices of the World Trade Organization, the United States Trade Representative should consult closely with the committees referred to in paragraph (1) regarding—

subparagraph.content: the details of the agreement;
the potential impact of the agreement on United States agricultural producers; and
any changes in United States law necessary to implement the agreement; and

paragraph.content: any agreement or other understanding (whether verbal or in writing) that relates to agricultural trade that is not disclosed to Congress before legislation implementing a trade agreement is introduced in either the Senate or the House of Representatives should not be considered to be part of the agreement approved by Congress and should have no force and effect under Unites States law or in any dispute settlement body.

subsection.heading: Funding.—
subsection.content: Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary of Agriculture shall use to carry out and expand the seniors farmers' market nutrition program $20,600,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2023.

subsection.heading: Program Purposes.—
subsection.chapeau: The purposes of the seniors farmers' market nutrition program are—

paragraph.content: to provide resources in the form of fresh, nutritious, unprepared, locally grown fruits, vegetables, honey, and herbs from farmers' markets, roadside stands, and community supported agriculture programs to low-income seniors;

to increase the domestic consumption of agricultural commodities by expanding or aiding in the expansion of domestic farmers' markets, roadside stands, and community supported agriculture programs; and
to develop or aid in the development of new and additional farmers' markets, roadside stands, and community supported agriculture programs.

subsection.heading: Exclusion of Benefits in Determining Eligibility for Other Programs.—
subsection.content: The value of any benefit provided to any eligible seniors farmers' market nutrition program recipient under this section shall not be considered to be income or resources for any purposes under any Federal, State, or local law.

subsection.heading: Prohibition on Collection of Sales Tax.—
subsection.content: Each State shall ensure that no State or local tax is collected within the State on a purchase of food with a benefit distributed under the seniors farmers' market nutrition program.

subsection.heading: Regulations.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may promulgate such regulations as the Secretary considers to be necessary to carry out the seniors farmers' market nutrition program.

subsection.heading: Federal Law Not Applicable.—
subsection.content: Section 920 of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act shall not apply to electronic benefit transfer systems established under this section.

section.heading: BILL EMERSON NATIONAL HUNGER FELLOWS AND MICKEY LELAND INTERNATIONAL HUNGER FELLOWS.

subsection.heading: Short Title.—
subsection.content: This section may be cited as the “Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellows and Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellows Program Act of 2008”.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this subsection:

paragraph.heading: Director.—
paragraph.content: The term “Director” means the head of the Congressional Hunger Center.

paragraph.heading: Fellow.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “fellow” means—

subparagraph.content: a Bill Emerson Hunger Fellow; or
Mickey Leland Hunger Fellow.

paragraph.heading: Fellowship programs.—
paragraph.content: The term “Fellowship Programs” means the Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellowship Program and the Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellowship Program established under subsection (c)(1).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: There is established the Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellowship Program and the Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellowship Program.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The purposes of the Fellowship Programs are—

clause.chapeau: to encourage future leaders of the United States—

subclause.content: to pursue careers in humanitarian and public service;
to recognize the needs of low-income people and hungry people;
to provide assistance to people in need; and
to seek public policy solutions to the challenges of hunger and poverty;

clause.content: to provide training and development opportunities for such leaders through placement in programs operated by appropriate organizations or entities; and
to increase awareness of the importance of public service.

subparagraph.heading: Bill emerson hunger fellowship program.—
subparagraph.content: The purpose of the Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship Program is to address hunger and poverty in the United States.

subparagraph.heading: Mickey leland hunger fellowship program.—
subparagraph.content: The purpose of the Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship Program is to address international hunger and other humanitarian needs.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall offer to provide a grant to the Congressional Hunger Center to administer the Fellowship Programs.

subparagraph.heading: Terms of grant.—
subparagraph.content: The terms of the grant provided under subparagraph (A), including the length of the grant and provisions for the alteration or termination of the grant, shall be determined by the Secretary in accordance with this section.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Director shall make available Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowships and Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowships in accordance with this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Fellowship Programs shall provide experience and training to develop the skills necessary to train fellows to carry out the purposes described in subsection (c)(2), including—

clause.content: training in direct service programs for the hungry and other anti-hunger programs in conjunction with community-based organizations through a program of field placement; and
providing experience in policy development through placement in a governmental entity or nongovernmental, nonprofit, or private sector organization.

subparagraph.heading: Work plan.—
subparagraph.content: To carry out subparagraph (A) and assist in the evaluation of the fellowships under paragraph (6), the Director shall, for each fellow, approve a work plan that identifies the target objectives for the fellow in the fellowship, including specific duties and responsibilities relating to those objectives.

subparagraph.heading: Bill emerson hunger fellow.—
subparagraph.content: A Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship awarded under this section shall be for not more than 15 months.

subparagraph.heading: Mickey leland hunger fellow.—
subparagraph.content: A Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship awarded under this section shall be for not more than 2 years.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Fellowships shall be awarded pursuant to a nationwide competition established by the Director.

subparagraph.heading: Qualifications.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A successful program applicant shall be an individual who has demonstrated—

clause.content: an intent to pursue a career in humanitarian services and outstanding potential for such a career;
leadership potential or actual leadership experience;
diverse life experience;
proficient writing and speaking skills;
an ability to live in poor or diverse communities; and
such other attributes as are considered to be appropriate by the Director.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A fellow shall receive—

clause.content: a living allowance during the term of the Fellowship; and
subject to subparagraph (B), an end-of-service award.

subparagraph.heading: Requirement for successful completion of fellowship.—
subparagraph.content: Each fellow shall be entitled to receive an end-of-service award at an appropriate rate for each month of satisfactory service completed, as determined by the Director.

subparagraph.heading: Terms of fellowship.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A fellow shall not be considered an employee of—

clause.content: the Department of Agriculture;
the Congressional Hunger Center; or
a host agency in the field or policy placement of the fellow.

clause.heading: Emerson fellow.—
clause.content: An individual awarded a fellowship from the Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship shall be known as an “Emerson Fellow”.

clause.heading: Leland fellow.—
clause.content: An individual awarded a fellowship from the Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship shall be known as a “Leland Fellow”.

paragraph.heading: Evaluations and audits.—
paragraph.chapeau: Under terms stipulated in the contract entered into under subsection (c)(3), the Director shall—

subparagraph.content: conduct periodic evaluations of the Fellowship Programs; and
arrange for annual independent financial audits of expenditures under the Fellowship Programs.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), in carrying out this section, the Director may solicit, accept, use, and dispose of gifts, bequests, or devises of services or property, both real and personal, for the purpose of facilitating the work of the Fellowship Programs.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: Gifts, bequests, or devises of money and proceeds from sales of other property received as gifts, bequests, or devises shall be used exclusively for the purposes of the Fellowship Programs.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The Director shall annually submit to the Secretary of Agriculture, the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives, and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report that—

paragraph.content: describes the activities and expenditures of the Fellowship Programs during the preceding fiscal year, including expenditures made from funds made available under subsection (g); and
includes the results of evaluations and audits required by subsection (d).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary such sums as are necessary to carry out this section, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.chapeau: The purpose of this section is to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a demonstration program under which agricultural producers are provided—

paragraph.content: technical assistance, consisting of engineering services, applied research, scale production, and similar services, to enable the agricultural producers to establish businesses to produce value-added agricultural commodities or products;
assistance in marketing, market development, and business planning; and
organizational, outreach, and development assistance to increase the viability, growth, and sustainability of businesses that produce value-added agricultural commodities or products.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “Program” means the Agriculture Innovation Center Demonstration Program established under subsection (c).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a demonstration program, to be known as the “Agriculture Innovation Center Demonstration Program” under which the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: make grants to assist eligible entities in establishing Agriculture Innovation Centers to enable agricultural producers to obtain the assistance described in subsection (a); and
provide assistance to eligible entities in establishing Agriculture Innovation Centers through the research and technical services of the Department of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: An entity shall be eligible for a grant and assistance described in subsection (c) to establish an Agriculture Innovation Center if—

subparagraph.chapeau: the entity—

clause.content: has provided services similar to the services described in subsection (a); or
demonstrates the capability of providing such services;

subparagraph.chapeau: the application of the entity for the grant and assistance includes a plan, in accordance with regulations promulgated by the Secretary, that outlines—

clause.content: the support for the entity in the agricultural community;
the technical and other expertise of the entity; and
the goals of the entity for increasing and improving the ability of local agricultural producers to develop markets and processes for value-added agricultural commodities or products;

subparagraph.content: the entity demonstrates that adequate resources (in cash or in kind) are available, or have been committed to be made available, to the entity, to increase and improve the ability of local agricultural producers to develop markets and processes for value-added agricultural commodities or products; and
the Agriculture Innovation Center of the entity has a board of directors established in accordance with paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Board of directors.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each Agriculture Innovation Center of an eligible entity shall have a board of directors composed of a diverse group of representatives of public and private entities, including the following::56

footnote.p: Two colons in paragraph (2) are so in law. See amendment made by section 7608(1)(A) of Public Law 115–334.

subparagraph.content: Two general agricultural organizations with the greatest number of members in the State in which the eligible entity is located.
The department of agriculture, or similar State department or agency, or a State legislator, of the State in which the eligible entity is located.
Four entities representing commodities produced in the State.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to subsection (g), under the Program, the Secretary shall make, on a competitive basis, annual grants to eligible entities.

paragraph.heading: Maximum amount of grants.—
paragraph.chapeau: A grant under paragraph (1) shall be in an amount that does not exceed the lesser of—

subparagraph.content: twice the dollar amount of the resources (in cash or in kind) that the eligible entity demonstrates are available, or have been committed to be made available, to the eligible entity in accordance with subsection (d)(1)(C).

subparagraph.heading: First fiscal year of program.—
subparagraph.content: In the first fiscal year of the Program, the Secretary shall make grants to not more than 5 eligible entities.

subparagraph.heading: Second fiscal year of program.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In the second fiscal year of the Program, the Secretary may make grants to—

clause.content: the eligible entities to which grants were made under subparagraph (A); and
not more than 10 additional eligible entities.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), in the first 3 fiscal years of the Program, the Secretary shall not make a grant under the Program to more than 1 entity in any 1 State.

subparagraph.heading: Collaboration.—
subparagraph.content: Nothing in subparagraph (A) precludes a recipient of a grant under the Program from collaborating with any other institution with respect to activities conducted using the grant.

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.chapeau: An eligible entity to which a grant is made under the Program may use the grant only for the following purposes (but only to the extent that the use is not described in section 210A(d)(5)(D) of the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946:

paragraph.content: Applied research.
Consulting services.
Hiring of employees, at the discretion of the board of directors of the Agriculture Innovation Center of the eligible entity.

The making of matching grants, each of which shall be in an amount not to exceed $5,000, to agricultural producers, except that the aggregate amount of all such matching grants made by the eligible entity shall be not more than $50,000.
Legal services.
Any other related cost, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023. * * * * * * *

section.heading: RURAL FIREFIGHTERS AND EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Definition of Emergency Medical Services.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “emergency medical services” means resources used by a public or nonprofit entity to deliver medical care outside of a medical facility under emergency conditions that occur as a result of—

subparagraph.content: the condition of a patient; or
a natural disaster or related condition.

paragraph.heading: Inclusion.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “emergency medical services” includes services (whether compensated or volunteer) delivered by an emergency medical services provider or other provider recognized by the State involved that is licensed or certified by the State as—

subparagraph.content: an emergency medical technician or the equivalent (as determined by the State);
a registered nurse;
a physician assistant; or
a physician that provides services similar to services provided by such an emergency medical services provider.

subsection.heading: Grants.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall award grants to eligible entities—

paragraph.content: to enable the entities to provide for improved emergency medical services in rural areas; and
to pay the cost of training firefighters and emergency medical personnel in firefighting, emergency medical practices, and responding to hazardous materials and bioagents in rural areas.

subsection.heading: Eligibility.—
subsection.chapeau: To be eligible to receive a grant under this section, an entity shall—

paragraph.chapeau: be—

subparagraph.content: a State emergency medical services office;
a State emergency medical services association;
a State office of rural health or an equivalent agency;
a local government entity;
an Indian tribe (as defined in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 450b));
a State or local ambulance provider; or
any other public or nonprofit entity determined appropriate by the Secretary; and

paragraph.chapeau: prepare and submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, that includes—

subparagraph.content: a description of the activities to be carried out under the grant; and
an assurance that the applicant will comply with the matching requirement of subsection (f).

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.chapeau: An entity shall use amounts received under a grant made under subsection (b) only in a rural area—

paragraph.content: to hire or recruit emergency medical service personnel;
to recruit or retain volunteer emergency medical service personnel;
to train emergency medical service personnel in emergency response, injury prevention, safety awareness, or other topics relevant to the delivery of emergency medical services;
to fund training to meet State or Federal certification requirements;
to provide training for firefighters or emergency medical personnel for improvements to the training facility, equipment, curricula, or personnel;
to develop new ways to educate emergency health care providers through the use of technology-enhanced educational methods (such as distance learning);
to acquire emergency medical services vehicles, including ambulances;
to acquire emergency medical services equipment, including cardiac defibrillators;
to acquire personal protective equipment for emergency medical services personnel as required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration; or
to educate the public concerning cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), first aid, injury prevention, safety awareness, illness prevention, or other related emergency preparedness topics.

subsection.heading: Preference.—
subsection.chapeau: In awarding grants under this section, the Secretary shall give preference to—

paragraph.content: applications that reflect a collaborative effort by 2 or more of the entities described in subparagraphs (A) through (G) of subsection (c)(1); and
applications submitted by entities that intend to use amounts provided under the grant to fund activities described in any of paragraphs (1) through (5) of subsection (d).

subsection.heading: Matching Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may not make a grant under this section to an entity unless the entity makes available (directly or through contributions from other public or private entities) non-Federal contributions toward the activities to be carried out under the grant in an amount equal to at least 5 percent of the amount received under the grant.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section not more than $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2012.

paragraph.heading: Administrative costs.—
paragraph.content: Not more than 5 percent of the amount appropriated under paragraph (1) for a fiscal year may be used for administrative expenses incurred in carrying out this section.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS ON RURAL POLICY COORDINATION.

subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of Congress that the President should—

paragraph.content: appoint a Special Assistant to the President for Rural Policy;
designate within each Federal agency with jurisdiction over rural programs or activities 1 or more senior officers or employees to provide rural policy leadership for the agency; and

paragraph.chapeau: create an intergovernmental rural policy working group comprised of—

subparagraph.content: the Special Assistant to the President for Rural Policy, who should serve as Chairperson; and
the senior officers and employees designated under paragraph (2).

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.content: The purpose of this section is to help rural families and small businesses achieve cost savings by providing loans to qualified consumers to implement durable cost-effective energy efficiency measures.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible entity” means—

subparagraph.content: any public power district, public utility district, or similar entity, or any electric cooperative described in section 501(c)(12) or 1381(a)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, that borrowed and repaid, prepaid, or is paying an electric loan made or guaranteed by the Rural Utilities Service (or any predecessor agency);
any entity primarily owned or controlled by 1 or more entities described in subparagraph (A); or
any other entity that is an eligible borrower of the Rural Utilities Service, as determined under section 1710.101 of title 7, Code of Federal Regulations (or a successor regulation).

paragraph.heading: Energy efficiency measures.—
paragraph.content: The term “energy efficiency measures” means, for or at property served by an eligible entity, structural improvements and investments in cost-effective, commercial technologies to increase energy efficiency (including cost-effective on- or off-grid renewable energy or energy storage systems).

paragraph.heading: Qualified consumer.—
paragraph.content: The term “qualified consumer” means a consumer served by an eligible entity that has the ability to repay a loan made under subsection (d), as determined by the eligible entity.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Administrator of the Rural Utilities Service.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary shall make loans to eligible entities that agree to use the loan funds to make loans to qualified consumers for the purpose of implementing energy efficiency measures.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: As a condition of receiving a loan under this subsection, an eligible entity shall—

clause.content: establish a list of energy efficiency measures that is expected to decrease energy use or costs of qualified consumers;
prepare an implementation plan for use of the loan funds, including use of any interest to be received pursuant to subsection (d)(1)(A);

clause.chapeau: provide for appropriate measurement and verification to ensure—

subclause.content: the effectiveness of the energy efficiency loans made by the eligible entity; and
that there is no conflict of interest in carrying out this section; and

clause.content: demonstrate expertise in effective use of energy efficiency measures at an appropriate scale.

subparagraph.heading: Revision of list of energy efficiency measures.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to the approval of the Secretary, an eligible entity may update the list required under subparagraph (A)(i) to account for newly available efficiency technologies.

subparagraph.heading: Existing energy efficiency programs.—
subparagraph.content: An eligible entity that, at any time before the date that is 60 days after the date of enactment of this section, has established an energy efficiency program for qualified consumers may use an existing list of energy efficiency measures, implementation plan, or measurement and verification system of that program to satisfy the requirements of subparagraph (A) if the Secretary determines the list, plan, or systems are consistent with the purposes of this section.

paragraph.heading: No interest.—
paragraph.content: A loan under this subsection shall bear no interest.

paragraph.heading: Eligibility for other loans.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall not include any debt incurred by a borrower under this section in the calculation of the debt-equity ratio of the borrower for purposes of eligibility for loans under the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 (7 U.S.C. 901 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Repayment.—
paragraph.chapeau: With respect to a loan under paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.content: the term shall not exceed 20 years from the date on which the loan is closed; and
except as provided in paragraph (7), the repayment of each advance shall be amortized for a period not to exceed 10 years.

paragraph.heading: Amount of advances.—
paragraph.content: Any advance of loan funds to an eligible entity in any single year shall not exceed 50 percent of the approved loan amount.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: In order to assist an eligible entity in defraying the appropriate start-up costs (as determined by the Secretary) of establishing new programs or modifying existing programs to carry out subsection (d), the Secretary shall allow an eligible entity to request a special advance.

subparagraph.heading: Amount.—
subparagraph.content: No eligible entity may receive a special advance under this paragraph for an amount that is greater than 4 percent of the loan amount received by the eligible entity under paragraph (1).

subparagraph.heading: Repayment.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Repayment of the special advance—

clause.content: shall be required during the 10-year period beginning on the date on which the special advance is made; and
at the election of the eligible entity, may be deferred to the end of the 10-year period.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: All special advances shall be made under a loan described in paragraph (1) during the first 10 years of the term of the loan.

paragraph.heading: Accounting.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall take appropriate steps to streamline the accounting requirements on borrowers under this section while maintaining adequate assurances of the repayment of the loans.

paragraph.heading: Terms of loans.—
paragraph.chapeau: Loans made by an eligible entity to qualified consumers using loan funds provided by the Secretary under subsection (c)—

subparagraph.chapeau: may bear interest, not to exceed 5 percent, to be used for purposes that include—

clause.content: to establish a loan loss reserve; and
to offset personnel and program costs of eligible entities to provide the loans;

subparagraph.content: shall finance energy efficiency measures for the purpose of decreasing energy usage or costs of the qualified consumer by an amount that ensures, to the maximum extent practicable, that a loan term of not more than 10 years will not pose an undue financial burden on the qualified consumer, as determined by the eligible entity;
shall not be used to fund purchases of, or modifications to, personal property unless the personal property is or becomes attached to real property (including a manufactured home) as a fixture;

subparagraph.chapeau: shall be repaid through charges added to the recurring service bill for the property for, or at which, energy efficiency measures are or will be implemented, on the condition that this requirement does not prohibit—

clause.content: the voluntary prepayment of a loan by the owner of the property; or

clause.chapeau: the use of any additional repayment mechanisms that are—

subclause.content: demonstrated to have appropriate risk mitigation features, as determined by the eligible entity; or
required if the qualified consumer is no longer a customer of the eligible entity; and

subparagraph.content: shall require an energy audit by an eligible entity to determine the impact of proposed energy efficiency measures on the energy costs and consumption of the qualified consumer.

paragraph.heading: Contractors.—
paragraph.content: In addition to any other qualified general contractor, eligible entities may serve as general contractors.

subsection.heading: Contract for Measurement and Verification, Training, and Technical Assistance.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary—

subparagraph.content: shall establish a plan for measurement and verification, training, and technical assistance of the program; and

subparagraph.chapeau: may enter into 1 or more contracts with a qualified entity for the purposes of—

clause.content: providing measurement and verification activities; and
developing a program to provide technical assistance and training to the employees of eligible entities to carry out this section.

paragraph.heading: Use of subcontractors authorized.—
paragraph.content: A qualified entity that enters into a contract under paragraph (1) may use subcontractors to assist the qualified entity in carrying out the contract.

subsection.heading: Additional Authority.—
subsection.content: The authority provided in this section is in addition to any other authority of the Secretary to offer loans under any other law.

subsection.heading: Effective Period.—
subsection.content: Subject to the availability of funds and except as otherwise provided in this section, the loans and other expenditures required to be made under this section shall be available until expended, with the Secretary authorized to make new loans as loans are repaid.

subsection.heading: Publication.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 120 days after the end of each fiscal year, the Secretary shall publish a description of—

paragraph.content: the number of applications received under this section for that fiscal year;
the number of loans made to eligible entities under this section for that fiscal year; and
the recipients of the loans described in paragraph (2).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $75,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

subsection.chapeau: In this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Department.—
paragraph.content: The term “Department” means the Department of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Beginning farmer or rancher.—
paragraph.content: The term “beginning farmer or rancher” has the meaning given such term in section 2501(a) of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279(a)).

paragraph.heading: National coordinator.—
paragraph.content: The term “National Coordinator” means the National Beginning Farmer and Rancher Coordinator established under subsection (b)(1).

paragraph.heading: State coordinator.—
paragraph.content: The term “State coordinator” means a State beginning farmer and rancher coordinator designated under subsection (c)(1)(A).

paragraph.heading: State office.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “State office” means—

subparagraph.chapeau: a State office of—

clause.content: the Farm Service Agency;
the Natural Resources Conservation Service;
the Rural Business-Cooperative Service; or
the Rural Utilities Service; or

subparagraph.content: a regional office of the Risk Management Agency.

subsection.heading: National Beginning Farmer and Rancher Coordinator.—

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish in the Department the position of National Beginning Farmer and Rancher Coordinator.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The National Coordinator shall—

clause.content: advise the Secretary and coordinate activities of the Department on programs, policies, and issues relating to beginning farmers and ranchers; and
in consultation with the applicable State food and agriculture council, determine whether to approve a plan submitted by a State coordinator under subsection (c)(3)(B).

subparagraph.heading: Discretionary duties.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Additional duties of the National Coordinator may include—

clause.chapeau: developing and implementing new strategies—

subclause.content: for outreach to beginning farmers and ranchers; and
to assist beginning farmers and ranchers with connecting to owners or operators that have ended, or expect to end within 5 years, actively owning or operating a farm or ranch; and

clause.content: facilitating interagency and interdepartmental collaboration on issues relating to beginning farmers and ranchers.

paragraph.heading: Reports.—
paragraph.content: Not less frequently than once each year, the National Coordinator shall distribute within the Department and make publicly available a report describing the status of steps taken to carry out the duties described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Contracts and cooperative agreements.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out the duties under paragraph (2), the National Coordinator may enter into a contract or cooperative agreement with an institution of higher education (as defined in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001)), cooperative extension services (as defined in section 1404 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3103)), or a nonprofit organization—

subparagraph.content: to conduct research on the profitability of new farms in operation for not less than 5 years in a region;
to develop educational materials;
to conduct workshops, courses, training, or certified vocational training; or
to conduct mentoring activities.

subsection.heading: State Beginning Farmer and Rancher Coordinators.—

subparagraph.heading: Designation.—
subparagraph.content: The National Coordinator, in consultation with State food and agriculture councils and directors of State offices, shall designate in each State a State beginning farmer and rancher coordinator from among employees of State offices.

subparagraph.heading: Requirements.—
subparagraph.chapeau: To be designated as a State coordinator, an employee shall—

clause.content: be familiar with issues relating to beginning farmers and ranchers; and
have the ability to coordinate with other Federal departments and agencies.

paragraph.heading: Training.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall develop a training plan to provide to each State coordinator knowledge of programs and services available from the Department for beginning farmers and ranchers, taking into consideration the needs of all production types and sizes of agricultural operations.

paragraph.heading: Duties.—
paragraph.chapeau: A State coordinator shall—

subparagraph.content: coordinate technical assistance at the State level to assist beginning farmers and ranchers in accessing programs of the Department;

develop and submit to the National Coordinator for approval under subsection (b)(2)(A)(ii) a State plan to improve the coordination, delivery, and efficacy of programs of the Department to beginning farmers and ranchers, taking into consideration the needs of all types of production methods and sizes of agricultural operation, at each county and area office in the State;
oversee implementation of an approved State plan described in subparagraph (B);
work with outreach coordinators in the State offices to ensure appropriate information about technical assistance is available at outreach events and activities; and
coordinate partnerships and joint outreach efforts with other organizations and government agencies serving beginning farmers and ranchers.

subsection.heading: Authorization.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish in the Department the position of Agricultural Youth Organization Coordinator.

subsection.heading: Duties.—
subsection.chapeau: The Agricultural Youth Organization Coordinator shall—

paragraph.content: promote the role of youth-serving organizations and school-based agricultural education in motivating and preparing young people to pursue careers in the agriculture, food, and natural resources systems;
work to help build youth awareness of the reach and importance of agriculture, across a diversity of fields and disciplines;

identify short-term and long-term interests of the Department and provide opportunities, resources, input, and coordination with programs and agencies of the Department to youth-serving organizations and school-based agricultural education, including the development of internship opportunities;

share, internally and externally, the extent to which active steps are being taken to encourage collaboration with, and support of, youth-serving organizations and school-based agricultural education;

provide information to youth involved in food and agriculture organizations concerning the availability of, and eligibility requirements for, participation in agricultural programs, with particular emphasis on beginning farmer and rancher programs;
serve as a resource for assisting youth involved in food and agriculture organizations in applying for participation in agriculture; and
advocate on behalf of youth involved in food and agriculture organizations in interactions with employees of the Department.

subsection.heading: Contracts and Cooperative Agreements.—
subsection.chapeau: For purposes of carrying out the duties under subsection (b), the Agricultural Youth Organization Coordinator shall consult with the cooperative extension and the land-grant university systems, and may enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with the research centers of the Agricultural Research Service, cooperative extension and the land-grant university systems, non-land-grant colleges of agriculture, or nonprofit organizations for—

paragraph.content: the conduct of regional research on the profitability of small farms;
the development of educational materials;
the conduct of workshops, courses, and certified vocational training;
the conduct of mentoring activities; or
the provision of internship opportunities.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS REGARDING DOUBLING OF FUNDING FOR AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH.

subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of Congress that—

paragraph.content: Federal funding for food and agricultural research has been essentially constant for 2 decades, putting at risk the scientific base on which food and agricultural advances have been made;

the resulting increase in the relative proportion of private sector, industry investments in food and agricultural research has led to questions about the independence and objectivity of research and outreach conducted by the Federal and university research sectors; and

paragraph.chapeau: funding for food and agricultural research should be at least doubled over the next 5 fiscal years—

subparagraph.content: to restore the balance between public and private sector funding for food and agricultural research; and
to maintain the scientific base on which food and agricultural advances are made.

section.heading: ORGANIC PRODUCTION AND MARKET DATA INITIATIVES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall collect and report data on the production and marketing of organic agricultural products.

subsection.heading: Requirements.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall, at a minimum—

paragraph.content: collect and distribute comprehensive reporting of prices relating to organically produced agricultural products;
conduct surveys and analysis and publish reports relating to organic production, handling, distribution, retail, and trend studies (including consumer purchasing patterns); and
develop surveys and report statistical analysis on organically produced agricultural products.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this subsection and annually thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report that—

paragraph.content: describes the progress that has been made in implementing this section;

describes how data collection agencies (such as the Agricultural Marketing Service and the National Agricultural Statistics Service) are coordinating with data user agencies (such as the Risk Management Agency) to ensure that data collected under this section can be used by data user agencies, including by the Risk Management Agency to offer price elections for all organic crops; and
identifies any additional production and marketing data needs.

paragraph.heading: Mandatory funding.—
paragraph.chapeau: Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall use to carry out this section, to remain available until expended—

subparagraph.content: $5,000,000 for each of the periods of fiscal years 2008 through 2012 and 2014 through 2018;
$5,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2019 through 2023;
$1,000,000 for fiscal year 2024; and
$10,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2031.

paragraph.heading: Discretionary funding.—
paragraph.content: In addition to funds made available under paragraph (1), there are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section not more than $5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2023, to remain available until expended.

section.heading: INTERNATIONAL ORGANIC RESEARCH COLLABORATION.
section.content: The Secretary, acting through the Agricultural Research Service (including the National Agricultural Library) and the Economic Research Service, shall facilitate access by research and extension professionals, farmers, and other interested persons in the United States to, and the use by those persons of, organic research conducted outside the United States.

title.heading: ENERGY

subsection.chapeau: Except as otherwise provided, in this title:

paragraph.heading: Administrator.—
paragraph.content: The term “Administrator” means the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency.

paragraph.heading: Advisory committee.—
paragraph.content: The term “Advisory Committee” means the Biomass Research and Development Technical Advisory Committee established by section 9008(d)(1).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “advanced biofuel” means fuel derived from renewable biomass other than corn kernel starch.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Subject to subparagraph (A), the term “advanced biofuel” includes—

clause.content: biofuel derived from cellulose, hemicellulose, or lignin;
biofuel derived from sugar and starch (other than ethanol derived from corn kernel starch);
biofuel derived from waste material, including crop residue, other vegetative waste material, animal waste, food waste, and yard waste;
diesel-equivalent fuel derived from renewable biomass, including vegetable oil and animal fat;
biogas (including landfill gas and sewage waste treatment gas) produced through the conversion of organic matter from renewable biomass;
butanol or other alcohols produced through the conversion of organic matter from renewable biomass; and
other fuel derived from cellulosic biomass.

paragraph.heading: Biobased product.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “biobased product” means a product determined by the Secretary to be a commercial or industrial product (other than food or feed) that is—

subparagraph.content: composed, in whole or in significant part, of biological products, including renewable domestic agricultural materials, renewable chemicals, and forestry materials; or
an intermediate ingredient or feedstock.

paragraph.heading: Biofuel.—
paragraph.content: The term “biofuel” means a fuel derived from renewable biomass.

paragraph.heading: Biomass conversion facility.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “biomass conversion facility” means a facility that converts or proposes to convert renewable biomass into—

subparagraph.content: heat;
power;
biobased products; or
advanced biofuels.

paragraph.heading: Biorefinery.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “biorefinery” means a facility (including equipment and processes) that—

subparagraph.chapeau: converts renewable biomass or an intermediate ingredient or feedstock of renewable biomass into any 1 or more, or a combination, of—

clause.content: biofuels;
renewable chemicals; or
biobased products; and

subparagraph.content: may produce electricity.

paragraph.heading: Board.—
paragraph.content: The term “Board” means the Biomass Research and Development Board established by section 9008(c).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “forest product” means a product made from materials derived from the practice of forestry or the management of growing timber.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “forest product” includes—

clause.content: pulp, paper, paperboard, pellets, lumber, and other wood products; and
any recycled products derived from forest materials.

paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian tribe” has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 450b).

paragraph.heading: Institution of higher education.—
paragraph.content: The term “institution of higher education” has the meaning given the term in section 102(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1002(a)).

paragraph.heading: Intermediate ingredient or feedstock.—
paragraph.content: The term “intermediate ingredient or feedstock” means a material or compound made in whole or in significant part from biological products, including renewable agricultural materials (including plant, animal, and marine materials) or forestry materials, that are subsequently used to make a more complex compound or product.

paragraph.heading: Renewable biomass.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “renewable biomass” means—
